backend_and_device_selection.how: the profile's compute_policy declares the ceiling (full: gpu required); the device itself is resolved at run time by the canonical trainers — prism_fas.synthesis.gpat_trainer.resolve_device and prism_fas.detector.trainer.resolve_device

current_plan_identities.note: both were built with learning_rate AMBIGUOUS and therefore skipped. Any approved interpretation changes these identities, and the changed identity is what a later full run must execute against

interpretations.title: Skip the learning-rate coordinate entirely
interpretations.why: §15.2.3 skips a scalar that is ABSENT or NON-APPLICABLE. For C4 and Track R no LR scalar is absent — three and two respectively are present and active — so the skip rule does not reach this case. It is what the search plan does TODAY only because the ambiguity is unresolved, which is a holding position rather than an interpretation

interpretations.consequence: the unelected groups are never searched; their LR stays at the inherited value for the whole envelope
interpretations.title: Elect one existing scalar as the learning-rate coordinate
interpretations.why: keeps exactly one coordinate, matching the frozen search order, and leaves the other groups at their inherited anchors — which is what 'all other coordinates remain at the current best' already does for anything unsearched. But nothing in the inheritance elevates one scalar above the others, so ELECTING one is an act of scientific discretion with no evidential basis. Appendix J places an unforced result-affecting choice in USER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED

interpretations.consequence: m=1.0 reproduces the inherited configuration exactly, so the anchor trial is unchanged from Version B
interpretations.inheritance_support: Version B's own schedules already behave this way. The detector's _lr_lambda returns ONE multiplier that LambdaLR applies to every group; GPAT's cosine schedule anchors each group on its own base under one shared shape. Treating the LR as a common multiplier over grouped anchors is the inherited semantics, not a new one
interpretations.title: One coordinate that scales every active LR group, preserving inherited ratios
interpretations.why: keeps exactly one coordinate and the same trial count as A, searches every active group, and changes no inherited ratio: the candidate is a multiplier m in {0.5, 1.0, 2.0} applied to every group's own anchor. It is the narrowest reading of a single 'learning rate' coordinate over a component whose inherited anchor is a vector. It is an INTERPRETATION of 'around inherited anchor x0.5/x1.0/x2.0' rather than the literal text, so it still needs approval

interpretations.consequence: C4 grows from 1 to 3 LR coordinates (+6 trials); Track R grows from 1 to 2 (+3 trials). Inherited LR ratios are no longer preserved
interpretations.title: Search each active LR group as its own coordinate
interpretations.why: the §15.2.2 search order names ONE 'learning rate' step. Giving each group its own coordinate inserts steps the frozen order does not declare — two extra for C4, one extra for Track R — and enlarges the search. §15.2.2 already classifies expanding a candidate set or starting a second pass as USER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED; adding coordinates is a larger change than either, and it also breaks the inherited ratios by construction

track_g.title: Track G has exactly one applicable LR scalar
track_g.why: not an interpretation and not a user choice. Track G instantiates no ConvNeXt, its backbone optimizer group is empty and is omitted, and backbone_lr controls zero parameters. head_lr is the unique inherited anchor, which is exactly what the frozen rules require

c4_gpat.scheduler: src/prism_fas/synthesis/gpat_trainer.py:40-53, per-group lambda anchored on each group's base
c4_gpat.why: all three groups are optimized by one AdamW under one cosine schedule. cosine_schedule anchors each group's decay on that group's own base LR, so the 2:1:2 ratio is preserved for the whole run except at the shared absolute min_lr floor

c7_detector.scheduler: src/prism_fas/detector/trainer.py:342-348 (_lr_lambda), applied to all groups by LambdaLR
c7_detector.why: one AdamW, and _lr_lambda returns ONE scalar multiplier that LambdaLR applies to EVERY parameter group. Version B's own detector schedule therefore already treats 'the learning rate' as a single shape scaled across grouped anchors, holding the 1:10 backbone:heads ratio fixed for the entire run

scalars.name: encoder_lr
scalars.note: encodes the spoof source's artifact appearance into z_a; a live component of the frozen C4 architecture, not a historical one

scalars.name: recipe_lr
scalars.note: maps the frozen 41-D conditioning vector to z_recipe. It is the only path by which a C3 recipe reaches the generator, so it is auxiliary in size but not in function

scalars.name: generator_lr
scalars.note: the residual generator itself: the component that produces delta_high and the artifact map

scalars.name: min_lr
scalars.note: an absolute schedule FLOOR, not a base learning rate. §15.2.2 names the learning rate and the warm-up fraction as coordinates; a decay floor is neither, and searching it would add a coordinate the frozen order does not declare

scalars.name: backbone_lr
scalars.note: the group is built from local_backbone.parameters(). Track G declares local_branch=off, so the group is EMPTY and parameter_groups omits it — backbone_lr then controls zero parameters
scalars.optimizer: AdamW (single optimizer, up to two groups)

modules: every trainable module that is not the local backbone: global_projection, fusion head, region fusion, prompt head, manifold projections, local_head
scalars.name: head_lr
scalars.note: the only LR group that exists under Track G, and one of two under Track R
scalars.optimizer: AdamW (single optimizer, up to two groups)

scalars.name: min_lr_scale
scalars.note: a relative floor on the shared cosine multiplier, value 0.0

scalars.name: backbone_lr (B00)
scalars.note: B00 is the inherited Version-B ConvNeXt-only baseline. It is not a Version-C track and no C4/C7/C8 row runs it. Listed so the audit is complete, and so its 1.0e-4/5.0e-4 values are not mistaken for the M9 detector anchors

lr_evidence.search_method: grep for every field matching [a-z_]*(lr|learning_rate)[a-z_]* across configs/, then trace each to the code that consumes it. Names were not trusted to imply semantics

version_b_tuning_evidence.conclusion: Version B recorded no learning-rate sweep. Every LR value is a single inherited setting, never a search winner, so there is no Version-B precedent that elevates one scalar above the others

m10_optimizer_group_shapes.meaning: Version B's own M10 evidence shows the backbone group being OMITTED for the local-branch-off row. The Track G case is not a new situation; it is the inherited behaviour

rationale: minimum deviation: keeps exactly one learning-rate coordinate, which is what the frozen §15.2.2 order declares, and the same 12 trials as A

strongest inheritance: all three anchors are byte-identical to Version B and all three groups are live; B is the only option that searches the learning rate of the whole component as Version B configured it
least added discretion: A requires electing one scalar over two equally inherited ones with no evidence to justify the choice; B requires no election at all
preserves optimizer-group relationships: the 2:1:2 ratio is held fixed, matching what the inherited cosine schedule already does
no envelope enlargement: unlike C, no coordinate is added
c4.what_the_user_is_accepting: that 'the inherited anchor' for a component with grouped learning rates means the anchor VECTOR, scaled as a unit

rationale: backbone_lr controls zero parameters under Track G, so the inherited anchor is already unique. Recording this as a user choice would invent a decision the frozen architecture already makes
the same five criteria as C4
additionally: the inherited detector scheduler ALREADY applies one multiplier to every group, so a common multiplier is the inherited semantics rather than a new construct
the 1:10 backbone:heads ratio is a deliberate frozen setting — a frozen-then-finetuned backbone at 1e-5 with fresh heads at 1e-4 — and B is the only option that does not disturb it

recommendation.consistency_note: recommending B for both C4 and Track R keeps one meaning of 'the learning-rate coordinate' across the whole pipeline. Approving different interpretations per milestone is legal but would make the two search plans mean different things by the same word
recommendation.if_the_user_declines_all: the envelopes stay as they are today, with the learning-rate coordinate skipped. C4 and C7 remain scientifically blocked and NEEDS_SCIENTIFIC_DECISION stands

per_scalar_classification.encoder_lr: D — controls a live component of the frozen C4 architecture (the artifact encoder)
per_scalar_classification.generator_lr: D — controls the actual GPAT residual generator
per_scalar_classification.recipe_lr: C/D — controls the recipe encoder, an active module and the only route from a C3 recipe into the generator

c4_gpat.why_not_unique: all three scalars control non-empty, simultaneously optimized groups of the frozen architecture, and together they cover 100% of trainable parameters. None is historical, none is inactive, and none is a superset of the others

track_g_resolution.reason: §13.4.1 makes Track G global-only and forbids instantiating ConvNeXt. PRISMDetector.parameter_groups omits an empty group, so the backbone group does not exist and backbone_lr controls zero parameters. Exactly one LR scalar is applicable, which is what a uniquely inherited anchor means
track_g_resolution.supporting_rule: §15.2.3 'absent/non-applicable scalars are skipped, not invented'; §15.2.2 'Skip inactive terms'
track_g_resolution.version_b_precedent: M10 row B01 recorded optimizer_groups == ['heads'] for the same structural reason
